para.verbatim:
embed:rst Moves 'root' of 'sibling' into this file, when #adoptable :raw-html:`
` :raw-html:`
` A mod may keep its buffers and most objects in one ``.ini`` and one object's `section`_ in another file of the folder; the file that binds the buffers adopts that `section`_ so the object is remapped with the rest. Every `section`_ the graph of 'root' reaches through ``run =`` is copied in, in the sibling's order, with each resource of the sibling a value names renamed with ``RemapRef`` -- the resource is declared again in this file under that name (#siblingRefs, #adoptedRefs: every key of its `section`_, so a buffer keeps its ``type`` and ``format``), and an undo removes only the declaration

memberdef.definition: void AGRemapCore::GIMIParser< K, V, KeyHash, KeyEqual, ParserBase >::addRowSteps
memberdef.name: addRowSteps

para.verbatim:
embed:rst Adds the standard row sets to the end of #deferredParseSteps, in this order: a copy of the parser's global graph is put in the groups (:cpp:class:`GraphCreate`); a :cpp:class:`ResRegCollect` over the keys that ever name a resource builds a graph of the resource `sections`_ bound anywhere (:cpp:class:`ResIdentity`: nothing renamed, no models) and a :cpp:class:`GraphCollect` reads their ``filename``; the declarations and every key of every `section`_ are collected off the global graph; both graphs are taken out again (:cpp:class:`GraphRemove`); and every key of the chosen objects is collected. A step added afterwards runs after these. The edits are owned by this parser :raw-html:`
` :raw-html:`
` The global graph is #globalGraph, so the parser must make one (#makeGlobalGraph). Call this once #modObjs is set: :cpp:member:`RowSteps::objs` is asked of each mod object here

` :raw-html:`

A reading edit changes no graph and keeps what it found -- :cpp:class:`GraphCollect` is the primitive -- and an edit that implements :cpp:class:`IParseResult` files its result in :cpp:func:`BaseIniParser::parseData` right after it runs. memberdef.name: objIdentityKVPs

para.verbatim:
embed:rst ``(mod object) -> the KVPs that IDENTIFY a section for it``, in the order they should be written -- empty for "cannot say" :raw-html:`
` :raw-html:`
` **Only used when this parser has to INVENT a section**, which it does when a mod is missing an object outright and a download has to be hung off something (see :cpp:func:`addDownloads`). A section built from nothing but the download's register is a ``TextureOverride`` with no ``hash``, and a ``TextureOverride`` with no ``hash`` matches no draw call -- so the file is fetched, written, referenced, and never used (for example, a Kirara mod with no face diffuse) :raw-html:`
` :raw-html:`
` Left unset, the invented section carries only the download's register, so a parser that never invents one need not provide it. Set, an EMPTY answer means the object cannot be matched at all, and no section is invented for it -- nor its download declared (CherryHuTao has no face hash, so a mod of hers without a face section used to get a face section with none). :cpp:func:`makeGIMICharParser` supplies it from the same maps its classifier uses, which is the point: the assets that let the classifier RECOGNISE a section are exactly the ones an invented section has to CARRY

para.verbatim:
embed:rst Builds the ``Resource...RemapDL`` `section`_ for one register's missing file, adds it to that register's own resource graph, and records the download the ``.ini`` file has to make :raw-html:`
` :raw-html:`
` The `section`_ is built **once per name**, not once per register: a ``.ini`` file can only hold one `section`_ of a given name, so one :cpp:class:`IniParseDownloadData` referenced from several registers (or several mod objects) contributes exactly one `section`_ and one download, shared by every resource graph that asked for it :raw-html:`
` :raw-html:`
` .. note:: Sharing one ``FileDownload`` object across two *different* :cpp:class:`IniParseDownloadData`\s is still not supported, for the same ownership reason -- give each its own

parameterdescription.para: The name of the mod type, used to name the section_
Which mod object's resource graphs this belongs to
The register whose file is missing
The download to build the resource for
The folder the .ini file lives in

simplesect.para: The name of the resource section_ to reference

para.verbatim:
embed:rst This class inherits from :cpp:class:`TemplateParser` The base of the two GIMI template parsers -- :cpp:func:`makeGIMICharParser` and :cpp:func:`makeGIMIComponentParser` -- holding the steps both take: whether a ``.ini`` (or a sibling ``.ini`` of the mod's folder) draws the character's mesh or binds its position buffer, the texture bindings a texture override carries onto an object's entry section, the sibling textures declared as this file's own resources, and whether the file's own targeted sections bind anything :raw-html:`
` :raw-html:`
` A subclass names the hash types a hash is filed under for it (#hashKeysOf) and fills #textureBindings, #siblingRefs and #adoptedRefs as it reads the mod
